# Trace identity across application boundaries

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `security-service-identity` · **Security & Identity** · Catalog level: architect

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S05-Q009](#S05-Q009)

<p>Draw the authentication and authorization flow from a SPA through a gateway and identity provider to backend APIs.</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Design an identity flow in which every actor’s credentials, permissions and trust boundary are explicit.</p>

<ul>
<li>Distinguish OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect responsibilities in the selected flow.</li>
<li>Draw browser-to-API and service-to-service identity interactions.</li>
<li>Choose credential storage or managed identity from actual platform and access requirements.</li>
<li>Bound permissions and verify allowed and denied operations.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

- [Decide access throughout the token lifecycle](security-token-lifecycle.md)
- [Separate browser and transport trust boundaries](security-browser-transport.md)

<p>Begin with the protocol’s responsibility, then follow the caller through the application. Service-to-service calls change whose authority is represented. Storage and managed identities describe how credentials are obtained; least privilege asks what that identity may actually do.</p>

<a id="S05-Q011"></a>

### S05-Q011 · Foundation

<p>What responsibilities do OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect have in an application’s identity architecture?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q011](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q011)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q011](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q011)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect at the level expected for application architecture.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain the actors and intended use of each protocol, then connect them to a login and API-access scenario. Avoid an exhaustive list of grant types.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Separate protocol responsibilities and apply them to one identity flow.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Discuss application architecture; name any chosen flow and verify its current official guidance before implementing it.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Draws actor interactions and distinguishes identity information from API-access decisions.</li>
<li>States what must be checked at a consumer boundary rather than trusting a protocol name.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Treating OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect as interchangeable names for login.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What questions would you ask before choosing a flow for a browser application?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q012"></a>

### S05-Q012 · Mechanism

<p>What changes when one backend service authenticates to another without a user actively logging in?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q012](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q012)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q012](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q012)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What changes for service-to-service authentication?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Identify whose identity is being represented and how the receiving service decides whether to allow the operation.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Explain machine identity and permission boundaries separately from interactive user login.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Clarify whether the call uses the service’s own identity or delegated user authority, and identify the deployment platform. Establish the deployed version/provider and consult official documentation before answering.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Traces credential acquisition, presentation and permission evaluation for the chosen caller.</li>
<li>Explains how credential compromise or excess permissions would be detected and contained.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Copying a browser login flow without identifying the machine caller or delegation contract.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would the design change if the downstream action must retain the user’s authority?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q009"></a>

### S05-Q009 · Application

<p>Draw the authentication and authorization flow from a SPA through a gateway and identity provider to backend APIs.</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q009](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q009)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q009](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q009)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Draw an authentication/authorization flow from SPA to gateway/identity provider to backend APIs.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>A SPA is a browser application that updates its interface without full-page navigation for each interaction. Show actors, request directions and the decision owned by each actor.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Explain an identity flow as explicit trust boundaries rather than a collection of products.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Clarify the selected protocol flow, browser credential handling and gateway responsibilities; do not assume the gateway replaces API checks. Establish the deployed version/provider and consult official documentation before answering.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Labels where credentials are obtained, presented and evaluated.</li>
<li>Explains a rejected request and how to verify the responsible boundary.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Drawing boxes without explaining who trusts whom or where access is decided.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What changes if a client reaches a backend API without going through the gateway?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q023"></a>

### S05-Q023 · Application

<p>How would an application authenticate to a cloud resource using a managed identity instead of an application-managed secret?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q023](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q023)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q023](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q023)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain secretless authentication using managed identities.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>A managed identity is a workload identity supported by the deployment platform. Trace how it is used and which permissions the target resource must recognize.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Explain secretless credential acquisition without overlooking authorization and platform boundaries.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use Azure as context; establish hosting support, identity type and target resource rather than assuming universal compatibility. Establish the deployed version/provider and consult official documentation before answering.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Traces identity selection, credential acquisition and resource access for the chosen environment.</li>
<li>Explains how to test denied access and handle an unsupported or local-development environment.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Claiming managed identity automatically grants access to every cloud resource.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you diagnose authentication succeeding while resource access is denied?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S05-Q010 · Trade-offs

<p>Where would you store application secrets, signing keys and tokens, and what access boundaries should protect each?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q010](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q010)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q010](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q010)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Where should secrets, signing keys and tokens be stored?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Compare the needs of a browser, backend process and deployment system. Explain why different credentials may require different handling.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose credential storage from threat, access and rotation requirements.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Distinguish secret material from public verification keys; identify storage provider, runtime and who needs access. Establish the deployed version/provider and consult official documentation before answering.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connects each storage choice to a specific actor and exposure risk.</li>
<li>Explains rotation or recovery verification without revealing real credentials.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Recommending one storage location for every credential without considering its consumers.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you rotate a signing key while requests continue?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q016"></a>

### S05-Q016 · Production decision

<p>How would you apply least privilege to an API caller and to the application’s cloud identity?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q016](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q016)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q016](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q016)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Apply least privilege to APIs and cloud identities.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Least privilege means granting only the authority needed for a defined task. Explain whose permissions you are designing and how you would verify the boundary.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Translate a required operation into bounded permissions and evidence.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use one API operation and one cloud-resource operation; distinguish caller permissions from deployment or runtime permissions.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Maps authority to the exact resource and operation required.</li>
<li>Includes a denied-operation test and a process for reviewing permissions as requirements change.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Granting an administrator role for convenience without defending the exposure or review plan.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What evidence would show that a service has permissions it never needs?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>An Angular SPA accesses an ASP.NET Core API through a gateway, and the API reads a cloud resource. Draw both identity paths and explain each decision owner, credential access and permission boundary. Include a direct-to-backend request and a denied cloud operation in the verification plan. Identify the actual hosting and identity provider before choosing provider-specific configuration.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Identifies the actors, protocol roles and distinction between credentials and permissions.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Traces both identity paths, defends storage and delegation choices, bounds authority and verifies bypass or denial cases without assuming platform support.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>A diagram or a managed-identity label alone does not show which credentials are used, who evaluates access or whether permissions are appropriately limited.</p>
